name: Pretexting & Scenario Building
description: A pretext is a fabricated scenario that gives you a plausible reason to be somewhere you have no legitimate right to be. Effective pretexts are built on intelligence gathered during reconnaissance — they reference real vendors the target uses, real departments that exist, real systems in maintenance. The more specific and accurate the pretext, the more resilient it is to probing questions. Scenario building involves scripting the full arc of the interaction: your opening line, your response to challenges, your behavior if pushed beyond your script, and your abort criteria.

blue.det: Post-incident review may reveal inconsistencies in pretext story; employees may report suspicious conversation after the fact.
blue.cm: Security awareness training on pretext recognition; verify all visitors through established process regardless of story; call-back verification for any unusual request; document all visitor interactions.

refs.t: Social Engineering: The Science of Human Hacking
